blocks.md: This lesson follows **Budgets and Ceilings** in *The Agent Harness* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, The Agent Harness, § Budgets and Ceilings
blocks.md: A repair trajectory that receives its fair share of model service on every round can still loop across dozens of failing patch attempts without converging, or launch a new model generation when an unbilled test job in flight has already committed the rest of its allowance. Fair scheduling and provider quotas govern how a trajectory shares cluster capacity at a single step, not how much total work one trajectory may accumulate or how much uncommitted liability it carries while background jobs run.

questions.q: The section **Budgets and Ceilings** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: The trajectory advances only along legal state-machine edges whose guards pass on a current record version, and admission commits atomically under the record lock before any request leaves the host (register before send).
Withdrawing a result's eligibility to inform the model never clears the operation's obligation, and no trajectory reaches a terminal state until every obligation is settled or explicitly transferred.
An operation's maximum additional charge is withheld at admission and released only when evidence settles the operation, so ambiguous dispatches stay reserved.

Supervision needs one authoritative per-trajectory control record, written only by the harness, holding contract, lifecycle state, accounting, grants, current invocations, the operation table, and a live plan.
